sections.assessment: Ooi,Foo,Ng,Tan,2013,ChemEngResDesign91,2721–2731. Graphical time/capacity pinch planning illustrated with hypothetical data. Literature covers capture technologies/energy penalties, storage/EOR, temporal optimisation and resource-service conventions. This paper's proposed method is graphicalCSCC plus algebraicCSCA, not a solvedMILP.

Reservoirs supply disposal service; plants demand that service. CO2 flows in the opposite direction. Reservoir development must precede use; unused storage service can be carried forward. Plants cannot postpone capturedCO2 disposal. Stable pairing is a heuristic except when capacity/life forces a change; economic/geographic evaluation is outside the demonstrated model.

Hypothetical plants total700Mt versus600Mt reservoirs. Time/cumulative-load graph is shifted horizontally to a time pinch. Claimed external200Mt, internal matching500Mt, excess100Mt are independently recoverable from the input timing. No instantaneous injectivity constraint is demonstrated.

Three hypothetical reservoirs nominally1240Mt versus1200Mt demand; annual staircaseCSCC identifies40Mt additional service and80Mt excess despite positive net capacity. Inclusive annual-bin counts apply to Tables3/4, unlike continuous-duration hypotheticalTable1.

Table allocations place external flows inyear8. Boundary-versus-bin timing convention needs explicit reconciliation before operational use.

DetailedCSCCs yield two stated10-connection options. All Table7/8 rows and diagrams inspected. Literal replays do not close per-plant demand; some exceed Table3 rates, and Option2 exceeds reservoirB total capacity. Do not repair schedules from plot/prose by assumption.
